title: Chlorite maximum contaminant level: 1.0 mg/L for systems using chlorine dioxide, three-sample set average

conditions: Community and nontransient noncommunity water systems using chlorine dioxide for disinfection or oxidation (141.132(b)(2))
exclusions: Systems that do not use chlorine dioxide are not required to monitor for chlorite; transient noncommunity systems using chlorine dioxide are subject to the chlorine dioxide MRDL in 141.65, not the chlorite MCL

claims.subject: Maximum contaminant level for chlorite
conditions: The 141.64(a) table lists bromate (0.010 mg/L) and chlorite (1.0 mg/L) together; this claim covers chlorite only
The chlorite MCLG is 0.8 mg/L (141.53), recorded as claim.dbp.mclg.chlorite on page dbp.mclg

claims.subject: Routine daily chlorite monitoring
claims.value: Daily samples at the entrance to the distribution system; any daily sample exceeding the chlorite MCL requires additional distribution system samples the following day

conditions: Community and nontransient noncommunity water systems using chlorine dioxide for disinfection or oxidation (141.132(b)(2))
exclusions: Systems that do not use chlorine dioxide are not required to monitor for chlorite; transient noncommunity systems using chlorine dioxide are subject to the chlorine dioxide MRDL in 141.65, not the chlorite MCL

claims.subject: Routine monthly chlorite monitoring
claims.value: A three-sample set each month in the distribution system: one sample near the first customer, one at a location representative of average residence time, one at a location reflecting maximum residence time
conditions: The term three-sample set is also recorded on page dbp.definitions (claim.dbp.definitions.chlorite-three-sample-set)
Community and nontransient noncommunity water systems using chlorine dioxide for disinfection or oxidation (141.132(b)(2))
exclusions: Systems that do not use chlorine dioxide are not required to monitor for chlorite; transient noncommunity systems using chlorine dioxide are subject to the chlorine dioxide MRDL in 141.65, not the chlorite MCL

claims.subject: Additional chlorite monitoring after an entrance exceedance
claims.value: On each day following a routine entrance sample that exceeds the chlorite MCL, three distribution system samples: as close to the first customer as possible, at average residence time, and as close to the end of the distribution system as possible

conditions: Community and nontransient noncommunity water systems using chlorine dioxide for disinfection or oxidation (141.132(b)(2))
exclusions: Systems that do not use chlorine dioxide are not required to monitor for chlorite; transient noncommunity systems using chlorine dioxide are subject to the chlorine dioxide MRDL in 141.65, not the chlorite MCL

claims.subject: Reduced chlorite monitoring
claims.value: Entrance monitoring may not be reduced; distribution system monitoring may be reduced to one three-sample set per quarter after one year with no individual distribution system sample above the MCL and no triggered additional monitoring
conditions: The system must revert to routine monitoring if any of the three quarterly distribution system samples exceeds the MCL or additional monitoring is triggered (141.132(b)(2)(iii)(B), second sentence, not quoted)

claims.subject: Compliance basis for the chlorite MCL
claims.value: Arithmetic average of each three-sample set taken in the distribution system, whether routine monthly sets or triggered additional sets

conditions: Community and nontransient noncommunity water systems using chlorine dioxide for disinfection or oxidation (141.132(b)(2))
exclusions: Systems that do not use chlorine dioxide are not required to monitor for chlorite; transient noncommunity systems using chlorine dioxide are subject to the chlorine dioxide MRDL in 141.65, not the chlorite MCL

claims.subject: Chlorite MCL violation
claims.value: The arithmetic average of any three-sample set exceeds the MCL; the system must notify the public under subpart Q and report to the State under 141.134
conditions: A single daily entrance sample above the MCL triggers additional monitoring; it is not by itself an MCL violation
